title: FiTS: Interpretable Spiking Neurons via Frequency Selectivity and Temporal Shaping
subtitle: Spiking neurons that learn which frequency to respond to, and when.
eventFull: Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)
summary: FiTS has been accepted to NeurIPS 2026 as a Spotlight paper, and as the first author I will be in Sydney in early December to present it at the poster session. If you are attending, please come say hello. I would love to talk about spiking neurons, frequency selectivity, and what biology can still teach us about network design. After the conference, I will update this page with questions from the session, key discussion points, and personal takeaways. See you in Sydney!

title: Fork-Merge Decoding: Enhancing Multimodal Understanding in Audio-Visual Large Language Models
subtitle: Research notes ahead of EMNLP 2026
eventFull: Findings of Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP)
summary: Giving an audio-visual model both inputs does not ensure that it uses the evidence a question needs. Fork-Merge Decoding separates audio and video processing in the first few decoder layers, then brings them together. These notes focus on the examples, the layer trade-off, and the limits of what improved.
